<reason>CON won a competitive debate by making the mandate’s core problem easier to vote on: social-graph transfer is other people’s relational data, and PRO never closed the resulting enforcement dilemma. PRO had the cleaner captivity/souvenir narrative and a strong asymmetry attack, but “already visible” and after-the-fact recipient liability did not answer CON’s accountability-boundary distinction or the rubber-stamp-versus-gatekeeping bind. That left the proposition looking like institutionalized harm or a new compliance moat, not a solved market fix.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R2/closing distinction that display and import stay inside the original platform’s consent and jurisdiction, while a mandated rival ingest does not—then forcing PRO’s registry into either scraper access or incumbent-only gatekeeping.</best_rebuttal>
